content_html:
Update: I couldn’t anticipate that my submission to HN would be so well received(for my standards). The story contiues here: HN discussion

First of all, a necessary disclaimer: I’m not a conspiracy theorist. Period.

Now that we have that out of the way, let’s talk about a theory that struck me this morning.

What if the RAM and GPU shortage is actually deliberate?

Deliberate by whom, you may ask? By the companies that depend on us subscribing to their services: the big AI companies.

But first, let’s look at some events that took place in 2025.

The rise of Chinese AI models

In January 2025, Alibaba released Qwen2.5, which shocked the tech industry with its performance. During the same month, DeepSeek-R1 was also released. Meanwhile, Moonshot AI was working on its own model, Kimi, which showed promising results.

All of the above(but especially DeepSeek-R1)caused havoc in the AI industry. Nearly $1 trillion was wiped from the tech market’s capitalization.

However, it wasn’t only the release of these models that caused concern. Chinese AI labs also released them under permissive licences, which meant that anyone could download and use them for free.

That alone was enough to cause panic in the AI industry, since its business model was suddenly under threat. Why pay for a subscription when you can run a free model with similar performance?

Then came the hardware shortage

By early 2026, RAM and GPU shortages were starting to be felt, although not nearly as much as by mid-2026.

For example, on 3 June 2026, I bought two 16 GB DDR4 RAM modules for €26.45 each. Currently, the same RAM is selling for €235.90 from the same online shop.

The shortages and price increases were reportedly caused by AI companies buying up as much RAM and as many GPUs as they could get their hands on.

Proper hoarding.

One could argue that this buying spree was necessary to keep up with the growing demand for AI services. But what if it also caused a convenient, accidental(or perhaps not entirely accidental)side effect?

If you, as a consumer or hobbyist, want to run a model such as Qwen2.5 or DeepSeek-R1 locally, you need a powerful computer with plenty of RAM and one or more capable GPUs.

If you can achieve a good number of tokens per second and get decent results locally, why would you continue paying for a subscription?

A convenient side effect?

If you were running one of those AI companies, how would you prevent that?

You would make sure that the RAM and GPU shortage continued, making it increasingly difficult and expensive for hobbyists and ordinary consumers to run these models themselves.

Simple as that.

Of course, the truth may be somewhere in between.

We have a saying in my country: kill two birds with one stone.

With one massive hardware-buying campaign, AI companies may have managed to accomplish two things at once: build enormous data centres for their services while also keeping RAM and GPUs scarce and expensive for everyone else.

Protection from Chinese competition

Recent reports also suggest that the US administration is considering restricting the use of Chinese AI models, including Kimi.

You can read more in this Axios article: US weighs restrictions on Chinese open-source AI models.

This is clearly a move intended to protect American AI companies, but it also suggests that they are genuinely worried about the competition.

In the end, we the users, may get the short end of the stick.

Hardware that was once widely available and relatively affordable has become scarce and extremely expensive. For now, there are few signs that prices or availability will return to normal anytime soon.

Let’s hope for the best.

更新：我没想到我向 HN 提交的材料会如此受欢迎（按照我的标准）。 故事在这里继续：HN 讨论

首先，一个必要的免责声明：我不是阴谋论者。 时期。

现在我们已经解决了这个问题，让我们来谈谈今天早上让我印象深刻的一个理论。

如果 RAM 和 GPU 短缺实际上是故意的怎么办？

你可能会问，是谁故意的？ 由那些依赖我们订阅他们的服务的公司：大型人工智能公司。

但首先，让我们回顾一下 2025 年发生的一些事件。

中国人工智能模型的崛起

2025年1月，阿里巴巴发布了Qwen2.5，其表现震惊了科技行业。 同月，DeepSeek-R1也发布。 与此同时，Moonshot AI 正在开发自己的模型 Kimi，该模型显示出可喜的结果。

上述所有这些（尤其是 DeepSeek-R1）都对人工智能行业造成了严重破坏。 科技市场的市值蒸发了近 1 万亿美元。

然而，引起担忧的不仅仅是这些模型的发布。 中国的人工智能实验室还根据许可发布了它们，这意味着任何人都可以免费下载和使用它们。

仅此一点就足以引起人工智能行业的恐慌，因为其商业模式突然受到威胁。 当您可以运行具有类似性能的免费模型时，为什么还要付费订阅呢？

然后就是硬件短缺

到 2026 年初，人们开始感受到 RAM 和 GPU 的短缺，尽管到 2026 年中期的程度已经没有那么严重了。

例如，2026 年 6 月 3 日，我以每个 26.45 欧元的价格购买了两个 16 GB DDR4 RAM 模块。 目前，同一款 RAM 在同一家网上商店的售价为 235.90 欧元。

据报道，短缺和价格上涨是由于人工智能公司购买尽可能多的 RAM 和 GPU 造成的。

适当囤积。

有人可能会说，为了满足人工智能服务不断增长的需求，这种购买热潮是必要的。 但如果它也引起了一个方便的、偶然的（或者也许并非完全偶然的）副作用呢？

如果您作为消费者或爱好者想要在本地运行 Qwen2.5 或 DeepSeek-R1 等模型，则需要一台具有充足 RAM 和一个或多个功能强大的 GPU 的功能强大的计算机。

如果您每秒可以获得大量代币并在本地获得不错的结果，那么您为什么还要继续付费订阅呢？

方便的副作用？

如果你正在经营其中一家人工智能公司，你会如何防止这种情况发生？

你会确保 RAM 和 GPU 短缺的情况持续存在，这使得爱好者和普通消费者自己运行这些模型变得越来越困难和昂贵。

就这么简单。

当然，事实可能介于两者之间。

我们国家有句俗话：一石二鸟。

通过一场大规模的硬件购买活动，人工智能公司可能成功地同时完成了两件事：为其服务建立庞大的数据中心，同时保持 RAM 和 GPU 对于其他人来说稀缺且昂贵。

保护免受中国竞争

最近的报道还表明，美国政府正在考虑限制使用包括 Kimi 在内的中国人工智能模型。

您可以在这篇 Axios 文章中阅读更多内容：美国考虑对中国开源人工智能模型的限制。

这显然是为了保护美国人工智能公司的举动，但也表明他们确实担心竞争。

最终，我们这些用户可能会吃亏。

曾经广泛使用且相对便宜的硬件已经变得稀缺且极其昂贵。 目前，几乎没有迹象表明价格或供货情况会很快恢复正常。

让我们期待最好的结果。
